## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the prep/audit-tier busy-signal contract pinned and the
duplicate-dispatch window closed by test, so nobody "fixes" the release by
re-introducing a claim-holder lock for prep tiers, and nobody re-opens the churn.

## Scope

Pin parent AC6 and AC7:

- AC7 (contract): a prep-tier dispatch (`/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`) has **no**
  `child-<id>.lock` claim holder, so pane evidence is the only signal. Assert the
  hydrator's `held` verdict is false for such an item and that the pane signal
  alone suppresses the release. The contract text lives in the `hydrator.ts`
  header comment (impl child) and is asserted here by behaviour.
- AC6 (no re-nomination): with the claim held and its pane live, the item is not
  returned to the dispatchable pool — it stays `in-progress` with the dispatcher
  assignee, so `wl next` / selection cannot nominate it on the next cycle. This is
  pinned in two layers: (a) drive a hydrate cycle against a cross-workspace pane
  and assert the item state is still claimed (item state, not just
  `demoted === 0`); (b) in `downtime-worker.gates.test.ts`, assert
  `evaluateCriticalFirstGuard` / the selection filters treat the claimed item as
  in-flight/held so it is not re-offered. Both layers are required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Parent AC6** — **No release storm / no duplicate dispatch.** After a dispatch, while its pane is live, the item is not returned to the dispatchable pool: a test asserts that a dispatched prep item is not re-offered/nominated on subsequent cycles while its pane exists (today it is re-offered every cycle). — Delivered here as the prep-tier tests plus the `downtime-worker.gates.test.ts` nomination case.
- **Parent AC7** — **Prep-tier signal contract recorded.** The chosen contract for prep/audit tiers (Root cause 2: pane evidence only, or a recorded claim holder) is documented in the hydrator header comment and covered by a test for whichever option is chosen. — Delivered here as the prep-tier pane-only contract test and the `hydrator.ts` header contract text.

- A test asserts a prep-tier item (no claim-lock file) with a live cross-workspace pane is not released, and documents in-line that the claim-lock backstop does not cover prep tiers.
- A test asserts the item remains `in-progress` with a non-empty assignee after the hydrate cycle, i.e. it is not returned to the dispatchable pool.
- A test asserts that when the pane is genuinely gone the same item IS released (the pair proves the signal, not a blanket hold).
- A `downtime-worker.gates.test.ts` case asserts the claimed item is not re-offered/nominated while its pane is live (the duplicate-dispatch window of parent AC6).
- No test relies on a real `flock`/`/proc/locks` read or a real `wl` spawn.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add cases to `hydrator.test.ts` (pane-only contract) plus, where cheap, a case
  in the downtime-worker selection/guard suite (`downtime-worker.gates.test.ts`)
  showing a claimed item is not offered.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/claim-lock.ts` (read-only: the prep-tier gap)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` / `downtime-worker.gates.test.ts` (nomination guard)

## Dependencies

None (test-first).

As the on-call operator, I want every release comment to carry the evidence that
justified it, so a future mis-release is diagnosable from the work item alone

Extend `buildReleaseComment` (and its call site in `runHydrationOnce`) to append

## Goal

Make the persisted per-prefix tab-anchor map **self-pruning**: when the map is
rewritten for a (possibly new) Dispatcher workspace, drop every `byPrefix` entry
that cannot belong to that workspace, so dead workspace ids cannot accumulate
and mask a later wedge.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC4).

## Context

`persistPrefixTab` upserts one entry and keeps `{ ...current.byPrefix }`
verbatim, so entries pointing into a superseded workspace survive indefinitely:

```json
{"workspaceId":"w6A","byPrefix":{"WL":{"tabId":"w6A:t2","paneId":"w6A:p5"},
                                "TCE":{"tabId":"w6A:t6","paneId":"w6A:p31"}}}
```

After a recovery to workspace `w6B` the map must not still carry `w6A:*`
entries: they can never resolve (the workspace is gone) and they make the
persisted state lie about where dispatch lands.

Herdr ids are workspace-scoped with a `<workspaceId>:` prefix (`w6A:t2`,
`w6A:p5`), so membership is decidable from the ids themselves — no CLI call is
needed and this stays a pure persistence-side change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `persistPrefixTab(dir, workspaceId, prefix, tabId, paneId)` writes a map
   containing only entries whose **both** `tabId` and `paneId` start with
   `<workspaceId>:` — plus the upserted entry (itself validated the same way).
2. An entry whose ids belong to a different (dead) workspace is dropped on the
   next write; the surviving same-workspace entries for other prefixes are
   preserved.
3. The map-level `workspaceId` is always the workspace being written (never a
   stale id).
4. **Stale prefix entries pruned.** Rewriting the tab-anchor map drops
   `byPrefix` entries whose workspace id is the dead one; a test asserts the
   persisted file after recovery contains no `w6A`-style dead ids (seeded from
   the recorded pre-fix map) and does contain the recovered workspace's entry.
5. Test: two prefixes in the same live workspace are both retained across a
   rewrite (pruning never drops a live sibling entry).
6. An ill-formed id (no `<workspaceId>:` prefix, e.g. a hand-edited file) is
   dropped rather than retained — it can never resolve in that workspace.
7. The write remains atomic (tmp + rename) and fail-closed (`false` on any
   error), exactly as today; no `wl`/herdr spawn is added.
8. Existing tab-anchor persistence suites stay green.

## Minimal Implementation

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts`: in `persistPrefixTab`,
  build `byPrefix` by filtering `current.byPrefix` on
  `tabId.startsWith(`${workspaceId}:`) && paneId.startsWith(`${workspaceId}:`)`
  before upserting; keep `writeTabAnchors` as-is (a `writeTabAnchors` caller that
  passes an explicit map keeps full control).
- Tests in `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` (persistence describe
  block) for AC2–AC6.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.persistence.ts` — the prune rule.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.test.ts` — persistence tests.

## Dependencies

- `Test: pin healthy anchor paths` (tests first).
- `Validate persisted workspace on read and re-provision` (AC4's post-recovery
  assertion runs through the recovery path).

## Out of scope

- Purging dead entries for workspaces that are still alive (only id-membership
  pruning is in scope here).
- Any TTL/reaper job; recovery remains on-read validation.

## Impact

After a workspace recovery, rewriting the per-prefix tab-anchor map now prunes
entries owned by the dead workspace, so stale ids can no longer accumulate and
the persisted map truthfully reflects where dispatches land.

## Goal

Make a genuine `anchor-unavailable` refusal **diagnosable from the log alone**:
carry a machine-readable detail naming the failing boundary (persisted workspace
missing vs unreadable herdr vs item-tab unavailable …) from the placement
resolver through to the `no-dispatch` decision entry.

Parent: WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (parent AC6; parent "Proposed fix B").

## Context

`resolveDispatchPlacement` collapses every failure into `{ ok: false }`, and
`abortForAnchorUnavailable` records the flat reason `anchor-unavailable`. In the
reported incident the log showed 124 identical `anchor-unavailable` entries with
no way to tell a vanished workspace from a broken CLI — which is a large part of
why the wedge went undiagnosed for hours.

The decision-log entry schema (`CoordinationLogEntry` in
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts`) is additive/optional by
convention, so a new optional `detail` field is compatible with every existing
entry shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `DispatchPlacementResult`'s failure variant carries
   `detail: PlacementFailureDetail` — a string union of at least
   `persisted-workspace-missing`, `herdr-unreadable`,
   `dispatcher-workspace-unprovisionable`, `prefix-empty`, `item-tab-unavailable`
   (extended by the sibling mismatch item with `project-workspace-mismatch`).
2. The detail is collected from the anchor resolvers without changing their
   existing signatures for current callers — an **optional trailing report
   callback** on `getDispatcherTabAnchor` / `getDispatcherAnchor`
   (additive; callers that pass no callback behave exactly as today), collected
   inside `resolveDispatchPlacement` so no cross-dispatch state is introduced.
3. The recovery outcome from the sibling fix item maps to the detail correctly: a
   workspace observed **missing** that recovers successfully yields `{ok:true}`
   (no detail recorded); a probe that is **unreadable** yields
   `detail: herdr-unreadable`; a persisted workspace positively missing whose
   replacement cannot be provisioned yields
   `dispatcher-workspace-unprovisionable`.
4. `DowntimeDispatchOutcome` for a placement abort carries the detail, and the
   `no-dispatch` decision entry records it (additive `detail?: string` field);
   `reason` stays `anchor-unavailable` so every existing consumer, budget and
   starvation heuristic is unchanged.
5. **Diagnosable refusal (parent AC6).** When placement genuinely fails closed,
   the `anchor-unavailable` decision entry includes a machine-readable detail
   naming the failing boundary (`persisted-workspace-missing` vs
   `herdr-unreadable`), and a test asserts the field is present. The stale-anchor
   state with an unreadable probe records `detail: 'herdr-unreadable'`; the
   prefix-empty and item-tab-unavailable paths each record their own detail.
6. Tests assert `reason` is still `anchor-unavailable` and the claim rollback /
   host-budget release behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.
7. No new barrel export, no changed export kind (split guard green), no `wl`
   spawn added.

## Minimal Implementation

- **Barrel-surface constraint (must not be missed).** The split guard asserts
  exactly 38 barrel exports (`expect(exported.size).toBe(38)` in
  `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.split-guard.test.ts`) and the baseline is
  frozen, so `PlacementFailureDetail` must **not** become a new barrel export.
  Declare the string-literal union locally on each side that needs it — a
  family-local alias in `dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` (not re-exported) and the
  union in `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — cross-referenced by comment;
  TypeScript's structural typing makes them assignable where they meet, so no
  consumer imports a non-barrelled symbol (which would also fail the
  "exports every symbol a live consumer imports" gate).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts`: declare the family-local
  detail alias and add the optional report callback parameter to the two resolver
  functions (type-level only; runtime behaviour is unchanged when no callback is
  passed).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`: report the boundary at
  each `return null` in `getDispatcherTabAnchor` / `getDispatcherAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`: create the local
  collector, pass it to the anchor resolvers, return `{ ok: false, detail }`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`: forward the detail
  through `abortForAnchorUnavailable` into the outcome and the decision entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts`: add the optional `detail`
  field.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` — collect + return.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — forward to outcome/log.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` — report boundaries.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — additive log field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — detail assertions.

## Dependencies

- `Validate persisted workspace on read and re-provision` (the classification the
  detail names).

## Out of scope

- The project-workspace mismatch diagnostic (sibling item).
- Changing the `reason` vocabulary or any budget/starvation heuristic.

# Refactor dispatched pane creation (WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

## Headline

Technical debt has accumulated across the dispatched-pane creation and management code: multiple parallel paths for discovering, creating and managing panes owned by dispatched processes. Review all paths, catalogue duplication/unification opportunities, and create one child work item per opportunity found, accommodating the naming needs of open in-flight items — stopping at review + child creation (no implementation in this epic).

## Problem statement

Dispatched panes (downtime dispatch, interactive dispatch, scheduled prompts, ship, fetcher, and their lifecycle management) are created and managed through several overlapping code paths that have drifted apart — e.g. two send-to-pi.sh argv builders with divergent option handling, three placement strategies for workspace/tab anchors, and fragmented pane-discovery/close logic. This makes maintenance riskier and each new pane feature touches many files.

## Users

- **ContextHub maintainers** — the primary users. They extend pane behaviour (naming, placement, lifecycle) and pay the cost of duplicated, drifted code.
- **Operators relying on the downtime dispatcher** — indirectly benefit: fewer pane-related regressions and a consistent naming scheme for workspaces, tabs and panes.

Example user stories:

- As a maintainer, I want one canonical send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh argv builder so a new pane flag (e.g. `--local-preference`) is added once and applied everywhere.
- As a maintainer, I want the pane-discovery and close logic unified so a span of behaviour change (e.g. the hydrator evidence fix) touches one module instead of four.
- As a maintainer, I want the naming scheme of workspaces, tabs and panes coherent with the open work items (e.g. `Ship` tab, `Dispatcher` workspace adopt-or-clean) so no future item needs to re-plumb naming.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — Review covers ALL pane spawn/management paths: downtime dispatcher (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`), interactive dispatch (`index.commands.ts` → `send-to-pi.sh` / `run-in-pane.sh`), scheduled prompts, ship-in-own-pane, fetcher spawns, anchor/placement (`dispatcher-anchor*.ts`), lifecycle/close (`pane-lifecycle.ts`, `pane-close*.ts`), and pane-capture (`index.pane-capture.ts`). Documented in the epic description.
- AC2 — At least one child work item per refactoring opportunity identified (duplication, configuration unification, code reuse, other smells), each under this epic with issue type and priority assigned: `critical` for items with significant maintenance impact, appropriate priority otherwise.
- AC3 — The review explicitly accommodates the naming/placement needs of open in-flight work items (WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ, WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR, WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU, WL-0MWHBSTM1004KQ49, WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW) — recorded in the relevant child descriptions.
- AC4 — Each child work item has a clear goal, testable ACs and predicted key files; children reference the specific code locations duplicated/drifted.
- AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (no behaviour change outside the refactoring).

## Impact

Maintainers can extend pane behaviour through fewer, unified code paths with a consistent workspace/tab/pane naming scheme, instead of patching several drifted implementations.

## Constraints

- Epic stops at review + child creation — no implementation in this epic; children implemented in their own sessions (operator decision).
- No behaviour change: refactoring must be behaviour-preserving; each child must keep the full test suite green.
- "Critical path" means `--priority critical` on high-maintenance-impact items, appropriate priority otherwise (operator decision).
- Scope is all pane spawn/management paths (operator decision).
- Respect repository boundaries: don't edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or agent-infrastructure dirs.
- Work must happen in the implement-skill worktree lifecycle (per child).

## Existing state

- `downtime-worker.pane.ts` — downtime pane identity, in-flight resolution, spawn invocation (via `send-to-pi.sh`) and lifecycle monitor. Contains `buildDowntimePaneArgs` and `spawnDowntimePane`.
- `index.commands.ts` — command routing + `buildSendToPiArgs` / `buildRunInPaneArgs` (agent and shell pane argv for `send-to-pi.sh` / `run-in-pane.sh`).
- `dispatcher-anchor*.ts` — three placement strategies (project workspace + item-ID tab; per-prefix tab in Dispatcher workspace; machine-wide Dispatcher fallback) + CLI parsers, persistence, herdr-cli subprocess helpers.
- `pane-lifecycle.ts`, `pane-close.ts`, `pane-close-cli.ts`, `pane-close-herdr.ts`, `pane-close-reaper.ts`, `pane-close-scheduler.ts` — pane lifecycle monitoring and close/reap paths.
- `index.pane-capture.ts` — pane-ID file capture and work-item ↔ pane association.
- `pane-title.ts` — shared pane-title builders (the exemplar of the desired unified pattern).
- `fetcher.cli.ts` — `wl` CLI spawn management with spawn cap (execFile, not send-to-pi.sh).

## Desired change

A documented map of all pane paths plus a set of child work items that, once implemented, converge the duplicated/divergent code onto shared builders/helpers (mirroring the `pane-title.ts` pattern) and a coherent naming scheme — without changing runtime behaviour.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — downtime spawn args/options + lifecycle monitor
- `packages/herdr/src/index.commands.ts` — interactive agent/shell pane argv builders
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor*.ts` — placement strategies, anchors, parsers, persistence
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — dispatched-pane lifecycle classification
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close*.ts` — close/reap/CLI paths
- `packages/herdr/src/index.pane-capture.ts` — pane-ID capture
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — canonical title builders (pattern to extend)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.cli.ts` — wl spawn management (potential unification target)

## Related work

- WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ — Hydrator releases a live dispatch claim seconds after spawn (open) — pane evidence workspace scope.
- WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR — Adopt-or-clean: orphaned Dispatcher workspaces (open) — naming/placement of the Dispatcher workspace.
- WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU — Ship opens in own pane (open) — new pane-spawn path + `Ship` tab naming.
- WL-0MWHBSTM1004KQ49 — Test: prep-tier pane-only busy contract (open) — dispatched-pane busy semantics.
- WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW — Host-wide release barrier (open) — dispatch pause across roots.
- Completed: WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU, WL-0MU7JZE04008VKP0, WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG, WL-0MTR2CD4X006XI7U, WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC, WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN, WL-0MU4URK4H006OFCE, WL-0MUKXFVMS001BP68, WL-0MUMA5OMH0024PN1, WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO, WL-0MW5JE0SZ0057K30 — prior dispatched-pane evolution.

## Risks & assumptions

- Scope-creep risk: the review may surface many small opportunities; record extra opportunities as additional child work items (or note them in a comment), not as scope of the epic.
- Assumption: refactoring children are behaviour-preserving; each child must keep the full test suite green (implement-skill gate).
- Assumption: "all paths" review may find paths the description did not anticipate (e.g. fetcher execFile spawns); these are in scope per Q1-A.
- Risk: open in-flight items (WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ et al.) change the pane landscape while children are being implemented; each child should pin which naming/placement contract it targets so the open items' needs are accommodated rather than re-litigated.
- Risk: a child that unifies argv builders may introduce subtle option-order or env differences; each such child must pin the exact argv/env delta with tests.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which pane paths are in scope for the review?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "A) All pane spawn/management paths — downtime dispatcher, interactive dispatch, scheduled prompts, fetcher, ship, pane-close/reaper/lifecycle." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q2: "After identifying opportunities and creating child work items, does this epic also implement any children?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "A) Stops at review + child creation; children implemented in their own sessions." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "Does 'critical path' mean `--priority critical`?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "A) Yes — priority=critical for high-maintenance-impact items, appropriate priority for the rest." Source: interactive reply (round 1).


## Review map (AC1 — all pane spawn/management paths reviewed)

Reviewed 2026-11-15 across `packages/herdr/src` and `packages/herdr/{shared,scripts}`. Every path below was read and its duplication/drift catalogued; each opportunity maps to a child work item (AC2).

| Path | Modules | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Downtime dispatcher spawn | `downtime-worker.pane.ts` (`buildDowntimePaneArgs`, `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `spawnDowntimePane`) | Drifted argv builder vs interactive; spawn env owns scrub+knobs alone. → argv child |
| Interactive dispatch | `index.commands.ts` (`buildSendToPiArgs`, `buildRunInPaneArgs`), `index.ts` call sites | Second/third independent argv builders, divergent flag sets. → argv child |
| Scheduled prompts | `scheduled-prompts.ts` + downtime spawn path (via `buildDowntimePaneArgs`) | Shares downtime builder — covered by argv child |
| Ship-in-own-pane | `WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU` (in-flight, plan_complete) | New `Ship`-tab spawn path; naming needs recorded in anchor + docs children |
| Anchor/placement | `dispatcher-anchor*.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` (`resolveDispatchPlacement`) | Three strategies with parallel provision-under-lock; live-pane-conditional primary path (traced root cause). → deterministic-placement (WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL) + anchor child |
| Fetcher spawns | `fetcher.cli.ts` (`runWl`), `fetcher.args.ts` | Third subprocess seam (execFile); duplicates binary-probe/error seams. → fetcher child |
| Pane lifecycle/close | `pane-lifecycle.ts` (disabled Mechanism B), `pane-close.ts` (shared classifier), `pane-close-herdr/reaper/cli/scheduler.ts` | Fragmented discovery + two close paths (one disabled, race documented). → discovery child |
| Pane capture | `index.pane-capture.ts`, `parsePaneIdFile` (`index.commands.ts`) | Single implementation — no duplication found (noted, no child) |
| Pane title | `pane-title.ts` | The canonical unified pattern the children should mirror |
| Label parsing | `paneLabelItemId` (×2) + `paneItemIdFromLabel` + `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` | Four graders, three semantics. → label child |

## Plan: children (updates)

- **WL-0MWHWGN23001KMQW** — Test: pin dispatched-pane spawn argv/env/placement behaviour (test-first gate for all unification children).
- **WL-0MWHW3PKX0048ZYL** — Deterministic project-workspace placement without live-pane dependency (folded in from the design-trace session; operator decision: "We want only one. Created in the same work tree." — an explicit placement behaviour change).
- **WL-0MWHWGZI4007D911** — Unify send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh argv builders (critical — significant maintenance impact).
- **WL-0MWHWH1HV009C46C** — Unify pane-label item-ID and kind parsing.
- **WL-0MWHWH6XL0025YX2** — Unify dispatched-pane discovery and close logic (critical).
- **WL-0MWHWH68L007L7IO** — Unify dispatcher-anchor placement strategies and CLI helpers.
- **WL-0MWHWHB3X004H9VG** — Unify fetch/wl spawn management with pane-close herdr CLI seams.
- **WL-0MWHWHBSW005KG13** — Docs: single pane-creation architecture map and naming contract.

Dependency order (test-first): the pin tests child precedes every unification child; label parsing precedes discovery + fetcher; deterministic placement precedes the anchor strategies child; docs lands last.

## Plan: changelog

# Deterministic project-workspace pane placement without live-pane dependency

## Headline

Dispatched panes land in the item's project workspace **only while a live herdr
`Work Items` plugin pane advertises the worklog root** via `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`
(read from `/proc/<shell_pid>/environ`). When that advertisement is absent at
dispatch time, `resolveProjectWorkspace` fails closed (`null`) and the pane falls
back to a per-prefix tab in a `Dispatcher` workspace — producing the two observed
placement behaviours ("created in the same worktree" vs "separate dispatch
worktree"). Unify placement so **every** dispatched pane is created in the item's
project workspace, deterministically, from durable data rather than live-pane
`/proc` scraping.

## Problem statement (traced 2026-11-15, session `herdr-1794749570-1465372-27601`)

The placement precedence in `downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts`
(`resolveDispatchPlacement`) already prefers the project workspace:

1. **Primary** — `resolveProjectWorkspace` (`dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`)
   enumerates machine-wide panes, keeps only `label == 'Work Items'`, reads each
   candidate's `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` via `herdr pane process-info` →
   `/proc/<pid>/environ`, and matches it to the item's worklog root. On a match,
   `getItemTabAnchor` ensures the item-ID tab in that workspace.
2. **Fallback** — per-prefix tab (`WL`/`AH`/…) in a `Dispatcher` workspace
   (`getDispatcherTabAnchor`).
3. **Retained legacy** — the single persisted `Dispatcher` anchor
   (`downtime-dispatch-anchor.json`).

Step 1 is **conditional on a live plugin pane advertising the root**. It fails
closed to `null` on any of: no `Work Items` pane carrying `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD ==
root` at dispatch time, an unreadable `/proc` env, a missing `shell_pid`, a CLI
failure, a match without a workspace id. Every such failure silently produces
behaviour 2 — a pane in a separate `Dispatcher` workspace whose `cwd` is still the
project root.

**Live evidence (ContextHub worklog, `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`):**

- ContextHub-root dispatches 2026-11-15 **01:18–08:29Z** all landed in
  `Dispatcher` workspaces: `w6C:p3`, `w6D:p3`, `w6V:p3`, `w60:p3`, `w71:p3`,
  `w72:p3`, `w76:p5` — while no ContextHub plugin pane was alive.
- The current ContextHub `Work Items` pane `w77:p2` started **12:41:01Z** with
  `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`.
- ContextHub-root dispatches after that (13:25Z → `w77:p6`, 13:29Z → `w77:p8`)
  landed in the ContextHub workspace item-ID tab `w77:t5` — the "same worktree".
- AI Hell items consistently land in AI Hell item tabs (`w50:t44`, `w50:t4H`)
  because that plugin pane (`w50:p8P`) has been up since 2026-11-14 23:29Z.

Root cause of the split: the same root may be advertised or not at any given
dispatch time, and fallback-placed panes stay open — so both behaviours coexist
in one pane grid.

**Registered-root sweep case (structural):** a `downtimeWorklogRoots` swept root
has **no running herdr instance by definition**, so step 1 can never succeed for
it — every swept dispatch is placed in a `Dispatcher` workspace (or fails closed).
A durable mapping fixes this class too.

**Directly affects WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ:** the hydrator's demotion-pane evidence is
workspace-scoped, so fallback-placed panes in the `Dispatcher` workspace are
invisible to it (the `w71:p3` implement pane for WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ is live
evidence).

## Operator decision (recorded 2026-11-15)

> "We want only one. Created in the same work tree." — every dispatched pane must
> be created in the item's project workspace. This is an **explicit behaviour
> change** for the placement scope and supersedes the epic's generic
> "no behaviour change: refactoring must be behaviour-preserving" constraint for
> this child (the `Dispatcher`-workspace fallback becomes a rare, logged
> last resort, not a routine alternative).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A dispatched pane for a work item is created in the item's project
  workspace (item-ID tab, existing adopt/reuse semantics) **even when no live
  `Work Items` plugin pane advertises the root at dispatch time** (plugin pane
  down, or a `downtimeWorklogRoots` sweep with no running instance).
- AC2 — root→workspace resolution is derived from a **durable source** (persisted
  per-root workspace map and/or the coordination registry's `worklogRoot`
  entries), not solely from `/proc` env scraping of live panes; the live-pane
  advertisement becomes a fast-path hint, never the only path.
- AC3 — The per-prefix `Dispatcher` fallback is retained only as a last resort
  (documented precedence unchanged) and **every fallback placement is recorded in
  the dispatch log with the reason**, so "separate dispatch worktree" placements
  become observable, rare and attributable.
- AC4 — Deterministic ambiguity: multiple candidate workspaces for one root use
  the existing focused-first then lowest-pane-id rule; adopted/reused item-ID
  tabs behave exactly as today (idempotent, no duplicate tabs).
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green; `dispatcher-anchor*.test.ts` and
  `downtime-worker*.test.ts` cover the no-live-pane and swept-root placements.
- AC6 — Naming/placement needs of the open in-flight items are accommodated
  (epic AC3): WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ (workspace-scoped demotion evidence),
  WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR (adopt-or-clean of orphaned `Dispatcher` workspaces),
  WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU, WL-0MWHBSTM1004KQ49, WL-0MWAM5N75004ROSW — no expectation
  re-plumbing.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` (`resolveProjectWorkspace`,
  `getItemTabAnchor`)
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` (`getPaneProcessInfo`,
  `readProcEnvironFile`)
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` (anchor/workspace types)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-placement.ts` (precedence,
  `resolveDispatchPlacement`)
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` (durable machine-wide state)
- Related: `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`

## Related work

- Lineage: WL-0MUR5FUWD00024XN (precedence fix — panes regressed into
  `Dispatcher`), WL-0MU321YK70035AYT (dispatch into project workspace),
  WL-0MUKXFX2M0019E3G, WL-0MWHCV3PR002WSQM (mismatch diagnostic, matching rule
  unchanged), WL-0MWHCUZ5C000I7S6 (anchor-unavailable refusal detail).
- Overlapping open items (not duplicates): WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR (orphaned
  `Dispatcher` workspace adopt-or-clean — the debris this fallback leaves
  behind), WL-0MWH50EN4007C6YH (stale persisted anchor re-provision),
  WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ (hydrator evidence visibility).

## Impact

Operators see exactly one dispatch-pane placement — the item's project workspace —
regardless of which herdr instance is running or when it restarted, with
`Dispatcher`-workspace panes relegated to a rare, logged last resort; the
hydrator's placement evidence (WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ) stops losing view of
fallback-placed panes.

# Unify send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh argv builders

## Headline

Collapse the three parallel TS argv builders — `buildDowntimePaneArgs`
(downtime dispatcher), `buildSendToPiArgs` and `buildRunInPaneArgs` (interactive
dispatch / shell panes, `index.commands.ts`) — onto one canonical builder per
script (mirroring the `pane-title.ts` unified pattern), plus one option parser
per shell script (`shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `scripts/run-in-pane.sh`), so a new
pane flag (e.g. `--local-preference`) is added once and applied everywhere.

## Goal

As a ContextHub maintainer, I want one canonical send-to-pi.sh / run-in-pane.sh
argv builder so a new pane flag (`--local-preference`, `--reservation-ticket`,
`--request-priority`, …) is added once and applied to all spawn paths — instead
of the today's drifted option sets (downtime builder carries
reservation-ticket/local-preference; the interactive builder carries
pane-id-file/request-priority; each has a divergent option order).

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

- `downtime-worker.pane.ts::buildDowntimePaneArgs` — `--pane-name`,
  `--no-focus`, `--anchor`, `--reservation-ticket`, `--local-preference`,
  `--cwd`, `--model`, then prompt.
- `index.commands.ts::buildSendToPiArgs` — `--focus|--no-focus`, `--cwd`,
  `--pane-name`, `--model`, `--pane-id-file`, `--anchor`,
  `--request-priority`, then prompt.
- `index.commands.ts::buildRunInPaneArgs` — `--focus|--no-focus`, `--cwd`,
  `--pane-name`, `--anchor`, `--pane-id-file`, then command.
- Shell-side: `shared/send-to-pi.sh` parses `--pane-name/--focus/--no-focus/
  --resize/--no-resize/--check-cli/--cwd/--anchor/--request-priority/
  --reservation-ticket/--local-preference/--model/--pane-id-file`;
  `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` is an *independent* option parser with a smaller set
  (`--cwd/--focus/--no-focus/--pane-name/--anchor/--pane-id-file`).
  `scripts/send-to-pi.sh` and `scripts/open-pi-agent.sh` are thin wrappers
  (canonical at `shared/`) — the desired pattern.

  (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`) owns scrub + knob injection; the interactive path
  has no equivalent builder.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — One canonical argv-builder module (e.g. `pane-argv.ts`, mirroring
  `pane-title.ts`) exports a single builder for `send-to-pi.sh` args and one
  for `run-in-pane.sh` args; `buildDowntimePaneArgs`,
  `buildSendToPiArgs` and `buildRunInPaneArgs` delegate to it (thin
  compatibility wrappers or direct call-site migration — no duplicated option
  assembly left).
- AC2 — The full flag matrix of all three current builders is supported by the
  canonical builders (per the pinned contract, test-first child
  WL-0MWHWGN23001KMQW: option set, order, defaults, env knobs), with a
  documented convergence decision per previously-divergent flag
  (pane-id-file/request-priority/reservation-ticket/local-preference).
- AC3 — `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` shares the canonical option parser (or becomes
  a thin wrapper over a shared `shared/` parser) — no second independent
  option-parsing implementation.
- AC4 — A new pane flag added to `pane-argv.ts` + one shell parser applies to
  every spawn path; the pinned argv/env tests prove byte-identical or
  documented-converged behaviour.
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green (split-guard baselines for
  `index.*`/`downtime-worker.*`/`fetcher.*` updated only where the extraction
  legitimately changes the public surface).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.commands.ts` — `buildSendToPiArgs`,
  `buildRunInPaneArgs` (migrate)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — `buildDowntimePaneArgs`,

  deliberately converged *and* documented (each such change pinned by test).

  where they exist today.

# Unify pane-label item-ID and kind parsing

## Headline

Collapse the three parallel pane-label parsers —
`paneLabelItemId` (`downtime-worker.pane.ts`, suffix-only, returns `null`),
`paneItemIdFromLabel` (`pane-close-herdr.ts`, regex-validated, returns `''`) and
the local `paneLabelItemId` (`host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts`, suffix-only) —
onto one canonical label-parsing module so a label-format change (e.g. the
hydrator evidence fix, WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ) touches one module instead of four.

## Goal

As a maintainer hardening the dispatched-pane evidence chain, I want one
canonical pane-label parser (item-id extraction + kind classification + label
prefix) so every consumer — downtime worker, reaper, host budget repair,
stalled-work, long-running-panes, ship guard, hydrator — shares identical
parse semantics.

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

Three item-id-from-label implementations with subtly different semantics:

- `downtime-worker.pane.ts::paneLabelItemId` — token after last ` - `, returns
  `null` when absent/empty; **no** shape validation (accepts any token).
- `pane-close-herdr.ts::paneItemIdFromLabel` — same suffix rule but
  regex-validates `/^[A-Z]{2,}-[A-Z0-9]+$/` and returns `''` when absent.
- `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts::paneLabelItemId` — local duplication of the
  suffix rule, returns `null`; comments admit "duplicated deliberately".
- Kind parsing: `pane-close-herdr.ts::paneKindFromLabel` (substring match over
  `PANE_KINDS`); `DOWNTIME_PANE_LABEL_PREFIX` matching is repeated at many call
  sites (`dispatch-claims`, `admission`, `stalled-work`, `long-running-panes`).
- ID *sets* in labels: `hydrator.ts::extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (regex over
  full text, used by ship guard) — a fourth parser at different granularity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — One canonical module (e.g. `pane-label.ts`, mirroring `pane-title.ts`)
  exports: item-id-from-label (single shape/return convention, documented),
  kind-from-label, label-prefix predicate (`isDowntimePaneLabel`) and
  extract-ids-from-text. The three existing implementations delegate to it; the
  local `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` copy is removed.
- AC2 — Return-convention divergence (null vs '' vs validated) is settled in
  the canonical API and every consumer updated; the pinned behaviour tests
  (pre-regex-validation on `paneItemIdFromLabel` vs suffix-only on
  `paneLabelItemId`) document which is authoritative and why.
- AC3 — All prefix-matching call sites use the shared predicate — no bare
  `label.startsWith(DOWNTIME_PANE_LABEL_PREFIX)` outside the canonical module.
- AC4 — `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (hydrator/ship-guard) is either moved into
  the canonical module or documented as intentionally different granularity
  with a shared regex constant.
- AC5 — Full unit + integration suite green; `pane-close-herdr.test.ts`,
  `host-dispatch-budget.repair.test.ts`, hydrator, ship-guard and stalled-work
  suites pin the unified behaviour.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — `paneLabelItemId`,
  `DOWNTIME_PANE_LABEL_PREFIX`
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — `paneItemIdFromLabel`,
  `paneKindFromLabel`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` — local `paneLabelItemId`
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-label.ts` (new canonical module)
- Consumers: `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`,
  `host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`,
  `long-running-panes.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`

## Constraints & assumptions

- Behaviour-preserving: parse outputs identical (or documented convergence with
  pinned tests). The regex-validation divergence on `paneItemIdFromLabel` is a
  deliberate safety net — decide authoritatively in the canonical API.
- Accommodates WL-0MWH56SWX004HSKQ (hydrator evidence fix must not re-plumb
  label parsing) and WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR (Dispatcher adopt-or-clean matches
  `Downtime`-labelled panes).

## Headline

Extract the shared plumbing of the three placement strategies —
project-workspace + item-ID tab (`dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`), per-prefix
Dispatcher tab and the machine-wide Dispatcher anchor
(`dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts`) — into a common find-or-provision-under-

helpers, so naming/placement changes land in one module per concern.

find-or-create-under-lock helper (and one herdr-CLI seam), so a naming/placement
change (e.g. the Dispatcher adopt-or-clean, WL-0MWHD0V41007ESWR, or the Ship
tab, WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU) is implemented once instead of three parallel
provisioning paths.

- `dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts::getItemTabAnchor` and
  `dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts::getDispatcherTabAnchor` /
  `getDispatcherAnchor` each re-implement the same

spawn cap, timeout, retry and in-flight memo) and the duplicated `herdr` binary
invocation helpers — with the canonical pane-discovery/herdr-CLI seams, so all
herdr/wl subprocess handling converges on shared deps factories and parse

close, budget repair, fetch) to share one CLI-resolution + spawn + parse
convention, so a change to the `herdr`/`wl` binary probe order or output shape
touches one module instead of scattered execFile/execFileAsync call sites.

## Problem statement (drift catalogue, WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ)

  bounded timeout, spawn-cap slots, in-flight memo) while
  `dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` and `pane-close-herdr.ts` each own their own
  `herdr` exec helpers — three subprocess seams with duplicated binary-probe
  and error-normalisation logic.
- `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` re-implements label parsing locally and
  shells out to `herdr pane list` through yet another path.
- The pane-close CLI bridges to the Python `pane-triage` skill via its own
  executable — the CLI seam is the cross-language contract that must stay
  stable.

  timeout, exec seam, error normalisation) is used by `fetcher.cli.ts` and the
  herdr invoke sites; the `wl`/`worklog` probe and the `herdr` probe each have
  one canonical declaration (constants shared, not re-declared).
- AC2 — Every `herdr pane list` invocation across the codebase goes through the
  single parse contract (`parseHerdrPaneCloseList` family); the
  `host-dispatch-budget.repair.ts` local label parse is removed in favour of the
  canonical label module (see pane-label child).

  unchanged and pinned by its fixture tests.

  the shared module header — no accidental convergence of unrelated seams.

  the fetcher suites pin the refactor.

  memo

  `getWorklogDir`

  `createHerdrReaperDeps`
